text: When your code doesn't work, the first step is to identify the bug. This means looking for the exact line or section causing the problem. Instead of guessing, use a systematic approach: check your code in small parts and test each one. Debugging tools are very helpful here. For example, a debugger lets you pause your program and inspect variable values. Logging is another useful practice—add print statements to see what your code is actually doing. By combining these techniques, you can trace the issue step by step, fix it, and avoid making random changes that could break other parts of your program.
